newsitem.title: GERMANY: German shares extend advance, banks dominate.
newsitem.headline: German shares extend advance, banks dominate.

text.p: Fortified by a firm opening on Wall Street, German shares extended their gains in afternoon trade to end strongly ahead on Tuesday, although anxiety about a possible U.S. rate rise inhibited activity.
The IBIS DAX index, which tracks electronic dealings in Germany's 30 blue chip stocks, ended the day up 72.36 points, or 2.2 percent, at 3,374.93.
That was some 25 points ahead of the DAX index's closing level in mid-afternoon at 3,349.14.
"Things looked unexpectedly calm in the U.S. and that made us more optimistic," said a Frankfurt dealer.

The advance was driven by bank shares, which hit the iimelight on Tuesday amid a barrage of criticism from unions and politicians for their role in trying to promote the first ever hostile takeover in the German steel industry.
Deutsche Bank AG ended the day up 3.47 marks at 91.92 marks, showing a strength which took dealers by surprise.

"The banks' performance is all the more remarkable given the disgraceful failure of Germany's first hostile takeover," said a dealer, referring to Krupp's decision not to go ahead with a bid for rival Thyssen and pursue a co-operation instead.
Shares in Thyssen plunged to end the day down nine percent at 375 marks while Krupp dropped 2.4 percent to 329 marks.
Shares in German builder Hochtief AG were lifted by an announcement that it and Deutsche Bank AG plan to pool their shares in Philipp Holzmann AG, Germany's largest builder.
Hochtief ended up 1.10 marks at 72.50 marks after the news, which is designed to sidestep German cartel office objections to it increasing its existing stake in Holzmann.
In general however, attention was fixed firmly on the Federal Reserve as markets awaited the outcome of its open market committee.
Dealers said a rate hike of 25 basis points had already been discounted by the German market. The outlook for Wednesday would depend on how accurate that forecast was and how Wall Street reacted.
BMW AG ended the day up 61 marks at 1,253 marks after the luxury car-maker said it boosted 1996 profits to 959 million marks and said it was out to increase its earnings power in 1996.
